Near-duplicate products and editions can make several matching history items represent one underlying preference; repeated item events amplify this further. Amazon’s historical dataset documentation explicitly reports merged reviews across near-identical products, including VHS/DVD editions; this establishes a plausible mechanism, not evidence that the pinned benchmark contains duplicates. Shared brand wording or description boilerplate can likewise inflate lexical agreement. Thus event count, distinct item count, and distinct product-family support should be measured separately. [Amazon dataset documentation](https://snap.stanford.edu/data/amazon/productGraph/)

Recommended training-only diagnostics: measure repeated-ID frequency, normalized-title duplicates, approximate title/description clusters, and event-versus-distinct-item-versus-cluster support within each 20-event prefix. Use metadata-derived clusters only for diagnostics or pooling ablations; preserve input splits. Compare title-only, description-only, high-document-frequency filtering, one-vote-per-item/cluster, and last-item-only residuals on internal chronological training holdouts. Report category-level results and residual magnitude by duplicate concentration; inspect whether gains survive removal of near-duplicate matches. These are proposed checks, not observed findings. TF-IDF downweights common terms, but shared wording within a smaller product family can remain influential. [TF-IDF documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/feature_extraction.html)

Implementation is realistic without an item-by-item matrix. Store normalized item TF-IDF rows in CSR; form each causal history vector from only the preceding 20 events, excluding its prediction target. Maintain rolling sparse sums by adding the arriving row and subtracting the departing row; apply normalization consistently. Score the positive and 32 negatives through candidate-row dot products, with negatives excluding the positive and permitted seen-item exclusions. For full-catalog inference compute blockwise Xh, add the collaborative score, mask seen items, and maintain top-k. CSR supports efficient row slicing and matrix-vector products; cap vocabulary/nonzeros and profile pooling, transfers, and output blocks. [SciPy CSR documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.html)
